reserveReview.rationale: The ousd API observation at 2026-10-30T19:10:33Z reports $904,709,499.27 of reserve assets against $902,709,381.85664 of aggregate on-chain liabilities (collateralization_ratio 1.0022), with two itemized components: $118,084,585.77 cash and $784,625,164.51 Treasury. The components sum to $902,709,750.28, so normalizing them gives 13.0811% and 86.9189%, which is 100.0000% without normalization. The itemized components exceed the on-chain liability by $368.42 (100.0000408%), inside the bridge-transparency adapter's unitemized-surplus bound and consistent with the documented CASH/OUSD rounding excess, and they remain $1,999,748.99 (0.2210%) below the published reserve total, which equals the issuer's stated $2,000,117.41 overcollateralization within $368.42 of rounding: the itemized line is the liability itself and the excess sits in the reserve line the issuer neither allocates nor names. The cash/Treasury split moves materially intraday: 55.7456%/44.2544% at the September 30 observation (components equal to both reserves and liabilities), 12.2272%/87.7728% at the 2026-10-29T18:30:39Z observation (when the components were $2,221,474.84 below a $828,870,912.65 liability, 99.732% coverage, and the adapter emitted bridge-itemized-backing-shortfall with effect degraded), 18.1240%/81.8760% at the 2026-10-30T10:40:40Z observation and 13.0811%/86.9189% at the reviewed 2026-10-30T19:10:33Z observation, so the weights are dated to the observation used and are not a stable allocation; both source keys and the very-low legacy risk tiers are unchanged. The Treasury category includes money-market funds comprised of T-bill ladders with less than three-month duration; it is not evidence of a hard maximum maturity for every instrument. The dashboard identifies Open USD, joinopenstandard.com, and the Tempo, Ethereum, Base and Solana deployments, and its attestation index lists only an August 2026 report for period 2026-08-31, which is not a same-period composition source. The second API slug open_usd is still frozen at its 2026-09-28T18:50:31Z observation ($40,008,735.98 liabilities, $40,008,737.98 reserves), its dashboard route returns 404, and it is absent from the documented ticker list; its contract identity remains unresolved and none of its balances are included here. These are issuer-published measurements, not an independent reserve examination.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Bridge ousd API cash and Treasury dollar amounts divided by their itemized $902,709,750.28 total; three-decimal percentage rounding
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The two published categories itemize the issuer's whole allocation chart, and at the 2026-10-30T19:10:33Z observation they exceed the aggregate on-chain liability by $368.42 ($902,709,750.28 against $902,709,381.85664, 100.0000408%). The remaining $1,999,748.99 (0.2210%) of the $904,709,499.27 reported reserve assets is neither allocated to them nor named, and it matches the issuer's stated $2,000,117.41 overcollateralization within $368.42 of rounding. Bank allocations, specific Treasury/MMF holdings, fund identities, provider shares, the composition and obligor of the unitemized balance, and any repo or tokenized-instrument suballocation remain undisclosed. The eligible reserve envelope permits additional forms but does not establish that OUSD holds them. Cash banking-hour access and Treasury one-business-day redemption are provider statements, not independently measured exit capacity.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: Bridge's OUSD-specific FAQ names BNY, BlackRock and Lead Bank as reserve institutions without allocations. Its reserve-management documentation identifies Lead Bank as the USD cash bank and BlackRock as an institutional money-market-fund and Treasury manager; the schema has no asset-manager role, so BlackRock is recorded as other rather than assuming securities custody. BNY's exact OUSD function, account entity and jurisdiction are not established by the fetched primary evidence, so its role remains other. The generic FAQ states segregated bankruptcy-remote accounts; binding terms require segregation from BBI operating assets but do not supply an OUSD-specific insolvency opinion or explicit rehypothecation prohibition. Terms deny token holders a property interest in reserve assets and limit redemption rights to eligible Bridge Users. No provider shares, independent custody report or OUSD-specific legal structure was published in the reviewed sources. The FAQ promises quarterly third-party transparency reports; a monthly independent OUSD attestation cadence was not verified. Section 2 of the binding terms entitles BBI to all net returns earned on reserve assets beyond the required minimum reserve, and Section 1 states the tokens are not designed to generate returns for holders. Open Standard's September 30, 2026 launch post says partners earn rewards proportional to the supply and activity they drive, so programme rewards flow to partners rather than to token holders (reviewed 2026-10-19).
